newsitem.title: SPAIN: Captivity ends for two held by Basque guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Captivity ends for two held by Basque guerrillas.

text.p: Two hostages held by the Basque guerrilla group ETA were freed on Tuesday, and police arrested four suspected separatist rebels, officials said.

Basque businessman Cosme Delclaux, who had been held for 232 days, was found drugged and tied to a tree near Bilbao. His family had paid his captors $6.85 million and agreed to pay a further $3.4 million after his release, police sources said.

Just hours after Delclaux's release, prison worker Jose Antonio Ortega Lara, an ETA prisoner for more than 500 days, was freed near the Basque town of Mondragon. State radio said he was rescued by police, but the exact circumstances were unclear.
Police said they had arrested four suspected ETA rebels after Ortega Lara's release.
Authorities said ETA had released Delclaux, 34, just after midnight following an anonymous phone call to the newspaper EGIN, which is closely tied to ETA.
He was found tied to a tree about 25 km (15 miles) from Bilbao near the town of Elorrio in the Basque province of Vizcaya.
He was picked up by a police patrol 15 minutes later and taken to a Vizcaya police station in the nearby town of Durango where he was treated by a doctor.
Police said Delclaux appeared disoriented possibly as a result of being given some type of sedative. He was said to have lost weight but was basically in good health.
In secret negotiations, Delclaux's family had already paid ETA the largest ransom it had ever received and had promised an additional payment after his release, police sources said.

Delclaux was kidnapped on his way home from work as a consultant at a multimedia firm in a Vizcaya technological park on November 11, 1996. Basque businessmen have long complained that ETA runs a campaign of extortion aimed at them.
Delclaux is a lawyer and the son of a wealthy Basque industrialist.
ETA, which stands for Basque Homeland and Freedom, has waged a 29-year struggle for independence from Spain in which 800 people have been killed.
Spanish news agency EFE said ETA had kidnapped 76 people since 1970 and 68 survived the ordeal.
